external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers. It calls the dispatch API and opens a WebSocket for live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: Runs hourly, pulls and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, archives the downloaded XML, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: Stores job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder containing each XML document downloaded by the schedule importer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The file store on which the schedule archive folder resides.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: load dispatch console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser and loads it from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser. ... our corporate web host serves it.

data_flows.name: call dispatch API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API across origins.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API. ... the API answers the console cross-origin.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to receive live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.

data_flows.name: read and write dispatch data
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS

data_flows.name: write schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded XML document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: downloaded XML documents containing planned work

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate and authority to move a crew or change depot work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane. The control plane is the same company and the same staff, but it is the zone that holds the live estate

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The trust zone controlled by the separate scheduling partner company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API is internally exposed because its production control plane is not reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the control plane where the dispatch API runs is not reachable from the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer is internally exposed because it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the schedule importer runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer presents a non-web interface because it is a batch-style importer that pulls, parses, archives, and posts data.
assumptions.basis: The text describes the importer as running hourly, pulling a feed, parsing XML, writing an archive, and posting work orders rather than presenting a web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database contains confidential data because it stores job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creator tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include personal mobile numbers and credentials alongside operational job records.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule archive contains confidential data because it stores downloaded planned-work documents and work orders.
assumptions.basis: The archive stores documents containing tomorrow's planned work.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate file store contains confidential data because it stores the schedule archive containing planned work.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the schedule archive is a folder on the corporate file store and contains downloaded planned-work documents.
